In my own memory, I carefully searched through the things I had experienced and the time that had passed, and I realized that only in the past two years have I truly felt that I am still alive. For more than a decade before that, I lived like a puppet. It was as if countless puppeteers stood behind me, and every single one of my actions seemed to be placed on a stage and controlled by them.

Only in these recent two years have I slowly begun to feel: I am also a person.  
I have started to have my own likes and dislikes, places I want to go, things I want to learn, stories I want to write, people I cherish, friends who make me happy, cats I can’t resist reaching out to pet, and those strange, wandering thoughts that surface at night or when I’m drunk.

I want to ask:  
“If I don’t live the way they want me to, what kind of self will I become? What do I really want?”

Looking back at the past right now, I realize I shouldn’t simply judge everything that came before as a “puppet life”—after all, I’ve only been alive for such a short time, haven’t I? Those years could be dark, they could be passive, but in the end they are only a small stretch within a much longer span of time. They have already passed, and I am now writing a new story.

As for those puppeteers, they may once have tied the strings very tightly, but I am no longer that puppet.  
I am learning, step by step, to walk on my own.

What I understand from the book is this:  
“Footprints do not need to be beautiful to prove that they are the ones you walked.”

Some footprints will be crooked, in some places you will fall, and on some paths you may even turn back. But when you look back, you can still say—  
“This is the path I once walked.”

All of this is what I felt after reading Mr. Keigo Higashino’s book,
Transformation

在咱自己的记忆里面仔仔细细地翻找了一下过去经历过的事情和过去的时间，感觉只有近两年才切实地感受到了自己还活着。前面的十几年都活得和傀儡一样，我的后面就像是站了许许多多的戏偶师，貌似咱的一举一动都像被摆上了看台被控制着。
只有近两年才慢慢感受到：咱也是个人。
我开始有自己的喜欢和讨厌，有想去的地方，有想学的东西，有想写的故事，有珍惜的人，有会让咱开心的朋友，有忍不住让咱去rua一把的猫猫，还有晚上或者喝醉的时候冒出的那些奇奇怪怪的想法。
咱想问：
“如果咱不按照他们想要的那个样子活，咱会活成怎样的自己？咱究竟想要什么？”
咱此刻回头看了看过去，其实不应该直接全部把之前的事情判断成“傀儡人生”——毕竟我只才活了这么短的时间不是嘛。它们可以是灰暗的，可以是被动的，但终究只是很长时间段里很小的一段。它们已经过去了，我现在正在写新的故事。
至于那些戏偶师，可能之前把绳子捆得很紧，但咱也已经不是那个木偶了。
咱正在学着一步一步自己慢慢走。
理解的书中的意思是：
“脚印不需要漂亮，才证明那是自己走过的。”
有些脚印会歪，有些地方会摔倒，有些路甚至会走回头路。但回头看的时候，咱仍然可以说——
“这里是咱曾经走过的。”
这些都是读了东野圭吾先生的《变身》这本书，后有感而发
